outline.chapter_title: Motivation: Aligning Language Models with Human Preferences
outline.description: Introduces the alignment problem for large language models (LLMs) and why unsupervised pretraining alone cannot ensure desired behavior. Frames preference learning as a practical route to steerability, safety, and usefulness.
subtopics: Capabilities vs. controllability in pretrained LMs
Why supervised demonstrations are insufficient or costly
Relative preferences as scalable supervision
Limitations of traditional RLHF pipelines (complexity, instability, cost)
High-level promise of Direct Preference Optimization (DPO)

outline.chapter_title: Background: Learning from Preferences and the RLHF Pipeline
outline.description: Presents the standard RLHF workflow from supervised fine-tuning (SFT) to preference data collection and RL-based policy optimization. Establishes terminology and notation used throughout the book.
subtopics: Three-phase RLHF: SFT → reward modeling → RL fine-tuning
Data formats: prompts, completions, pairwise preferences
Notation for policies, rewards, and datasets
Common RL algorithms in RLHF (REINFORCE, PPO) and practical issues
Why KL regularization to a reference policy is essential

outline.description: Explains probabilistic models of preferences used to learn from pairwise (or ranked) comparisons, focusing on their structure and implications for identifiability.
subtopics: Bradley–Terry (BT) model for pairwise comparisons
Plackett–Luce (PL) for listwise rankings
Logistic likelihood and binary cross-entropy interpretation
Underspecification: rewards identifiable only up to an x-dependent constant
Fitting a reward model by maximum likelihood

outline.description: Derives the standard RLHF optimization objective that maximizes expected reward while constraining deviation from a reference policy via a KL penalty.
subtopics: Objective: maximize E[r(x,y)] − β KL(πθ(·|x) || πref(·|x))
Role of β and the reference policy πref
Why sequence-level KL matters (prevent drift, retain diversity)
Challenges: discrete actions, variance, and on-policy sampling
Optimal policy form under KL constraint (exponential tilting)

outline.chapter_title: From Rewards to Policies: Deriving the DPO Objective
outline.description: Shows the central change-of-variables that maps reward functions to optimal policies, eliminating the need to explicitly fit a reward model or run RL.
subtopics: Optimal policy under KL constraint: πr ∝ πref exp(r/β)
Reparameterizing rewards: r(x,y) = β log [πr(y|x)/πref(y|x)] + β log Z(x)
Partition function cancellation inside BT/PL preference likelihoods
Policy-only likelihood of preferences
DPO loss: logistic loss on relative log-probability ratios to πref

outline.chapter_title: Mechanics and Intuition: What the DPO Update Does
outline.description: Builds intuition for DPO’s gradient update, connecting it to margin-maximization on preferred vs. dispreferred responses with adaptive weighting.
subtopics: Implicit reward: r̂θ(x,y) = β log[πθ(y|x)/πref(y|x)]
Gradient analysis: upweight examples where the model’s ordering is wrong
Why naive unlikelihood without weighting can degenerate generations
Effect of β on the strength of the KL constraint and learning dynamics
Connection to classification with example-dependent margins

outline.chapter_title: Practical DPO: Data, Training, and Implementation
outline.description: Details the end-to-end DPO pipeline and practical considerations to make it stable, efficient, and easy to use.
subtopics: Constructing the preference dataset 𝔇 from human/AI feedback
Choosing and initializing πref (SFT model or preferred-only MLE)
Training loop: batching, tokenization, loss computation, optimization
Hyperparameters: β, learning rate, batch size, sequence length
No on-policy sampling or value baselines; compute and infra savings
Troubleshooting: collapse, over-optimization, and monitoring KL

outline.chapter_title: Theory: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model
outline.description: Formalizes the equivalence between reward functions (up to an x-dependent constant) and policies under the DPO reparameterization, showing no loss of generality.
subtopics: Equivalence classes of rewards: r and r′ differing by f(x)
Same-preference and same-optimal-policy lemmas
Main theorem: any BT/PL-consistent reward class is representable as β log[π/πref]
Interpretation via partition-function-normalized rewards
Consistency properties under preference models

outline.chapter_title: RLHF Through the Control-as-Inference Lens: Why PPO Can Be Unstable
outline.description: Uses the DPO perspective to analyze actor–critic RLHF objectives and diagnose instability sources tied to normalization/baseline terms.
subtopics: Minimizing KL(πθ || π*) leads to an objective with a soft value baseline
Normalization term as soft value of πref and its variance issues
Difficulties of learning baselines/value functions in practice
Reward normalization tricks vs. DPO’s baseline-free reparameterization
When PPO may underperform despite optimizing the same target

outline.description: Summarizes empirical results demonstrating DPO’s performance, stability, and simplicity relative to PPO-based RLHF and alternative baselines.
subtopics: Controlled sentiment generation: reward–KL frontier comparisons
Summarization on Reddit TL;DR: GPT-4 win rates, temperature robustness
Single-turn dialogue on Anthropic HH: setup without SFT, Preferred-FT reference
Baselines: SFT, Preferred-FT, Unlikelihood, PPO, PPO-GT, Best-of-N
Compute and tuning effort: DPO vs. PPO

outline.description: Covers evaluation choices—reward/KL tradeoffs, win-rate comparisons with LLM judges, human studies—and out-of-distribution (OOD) generalization.
subtopics: Reward–KL frontier as objective-grounded evaluation
Win-rate against references; temperature sensitivity analyses
GPT-4 as an automated evaluator: prompt design and limitations
Human study: agreement with GPT-4 vs. inter-rater reliability
OOD evaluation: TL;DR-trained policies on CNN/DailyMail
Interpreting results and threats to validity

outline.description: Discusses where to apply DPO, open problems, and research directions spanning robustness, scaling, data quality, and broader modalities.
subtopics: When to prefer DPO over PPO-based RLHF
Scaling to larger models and datasets
Distribution shift and self-training with preferences
Reward hacking and over-optimization in DPO settings
Extensions to listwise preferences and other modalities (vision, speech)
Open questions for theory and evaluation
